# AI Inspection Platform for Insurance: Meet Inspect AI


More inspection photos don't automatically mean better underwriting evidence. If the required view is missing or the image is unclear, the reviewer still has to chase the customer before making a decision.


At AI Compass Lagos 2026, Curacel presented Inspect AI as the next step beyond Auto AI: an AI inspection platform for insurance built around a shared workflow, with asset-specific assessment. The[Inspect AI launch presentation](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XsUaU_PD9PsrJrtDW6ntWhiyDCUSkxOx/view) sets out that approach. Here's what it means for teams evaluating remote inspection.


**


## **What Changes When Auto AI Becomes Inspect AI?**


The point isn't to use the same checklist for every asset. It's to keep the inspection process connected while changing what each assessment looks for.


Curacel's launch deck presents four modules:


- **Auto:** Vehicle damage assessment covers severity. The launch deck also includes fraud checks alongside valuation and repair estimates.
- **Buildings:** Construction progress and occupancy assessment, with checks for hazards and defects.
- **Gadgets:** Cosmetic damage and functional tests, supporting grading and valuation.
- **Equipment:** Condition and safety assessment, including maintenance and compliance checks.


The launch presentation outlined four asset modules. Confirm the currently supported modules and implementation scope with Curacel when planning your pilot.


## **How Does the Inspection Workflow Work?**


The[Inspect AI presentation](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XsUaU_PD9PsrJrtDW6ntWhiyDCUSkxOx/view) separates evidence collection from the final decision. Its five-step workflow makes that boundary clear:


- **Capture:** Customers or field teams follow guided evidence collection.
- **Check:** Quality checks flag gaps and anomalies before review.
- **Assess:** Asset-specific AI examines the evidence for relevant damage, defects or hazards.
- **Report:** Structured findings reach underwriting and claims teams.
- **Decide:** People review the evidence and act.


For claims inspection automation, that distinction matters: an assessment isn't an approval. A reviewer still needs evidence that supports the decision, not just a faster report.


**


*From capture to report, Inspect AI structures the evidence. Your people review it and decide.*

## **What Stays in Place as You Add Assets?**


The deck's continuity proposition is that Auto AI customers retain their operating setup as modules expand. It identifies these shared elements:


- **Capture journeys:** Keep evidence collection connected to the platform.
- **Users and access:** Retain the existing access structure.
- **Integrations:** Preserve connections rather than introduce another isolated tool.
- **Reports and APIs:** Keep findings connected to downstream workflows.
- **Audit and governance:** Retain the controls surrounding the inspection process.


That builds on the operational problem in Curacel's article on[manual bottlenecks in motor insurance](https://www.curacel.co/post/auto-insurance-and-ai-battle-against-manual-bottlenecks?utm_source=curacel_blog&utm_medium=owned_content&utm_campaign=ai_compass_lagos_2026&utm_content=inspect_ai_slide_blog) . For a multi-asset inspection pilot, confirm exactly which existing connections remain usable and what configuration the new asset requires.


*The presentation’s continuity model keeps capture, access, reporting and governance within one platform.*


## **How Should Insurers Evaluate a Pilot?**


Start with one asset and one decision workflow. The following measures are an evaluation framework, not claimed Inspect AI results:


- **Evidence quality:** Track missing views and recapture requests.
- **Turnaround:** Measure elapsed time from first submission to a reviewable report.
- **Reviewer effort:** Record time spent resolving exceptions, not just reading reports.
- **Decision control:** Review overrides and cases still needing a physical inspection.


Agree on escalation rules before the pilot starts. Faster reports only help if reviewers can trust the evidence and know when to ask for more.


## **The Takeaway**


Inspect AI's proposition is a reusable inspection workflow, not one model that makes every insurance decision. Start with the evidence your team needs, test one supported module, and expand only when the workflow proves useful.
